speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our assessment, could you please describe the specific nature of your gait and limb ataxia, and when did these symptoms first appear?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the ataxia is more pronounced on the right side, I need to check for other focal neurological signs. Can you tell me if you have experienced any weakness, numbness, or changes in vision on that same right side?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and treatment with natalizumab, I am concerned about progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML). Do you have any cognitive changes, such as memory loss or confusion, or have you noticed any visual disturbances?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast.
REQUEST TEST: JC Virus PCR in CSF.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain: Lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML. JC Virus PCR in CSF: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI findings are highly characteristic of PML, but the negative JC Virus PCR in the CSF is unexpected and requires further investigation to confirm the diagnosis. I will request medical images related to the disease to be returned with "REQUEST IMAGES".

speaker: Patient
text: The walking difficulty and coordination problems are the main issues. I do not have chest pain or other major symptoms besides the neurological problems.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST IMAGES

The MRI findings are classic for PML despite the negative CSF PCR, so I will proceed with the diagnosis based on the radiological evidence and clinical context. DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML)
